fms_project_name: DEP - Variable Frequency Drives on Owl's Head WRRF Pumps
agency_project_name: Variable Frequency Drives on Owl's Head WRRF Main Sewage Pumps
agency_project_description: This project is to add speed controls to the replacement Main Sewage Pumps (MSPs) that will be installed at Owl's Head Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF). MSPs are the largest pumps in a WRRF and are used to bring flow to the plant from the influent well to the process tanks. The pumps used at Owl's Head WRRF are driven by 700 HP motors and are capable of pumping 60 million gallons per day (MGD). The scope of work for which this application requests funding is for the addition of Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) to the MSPs. This will include the HVAC upgrades required to cool the VFDs.

The project scope includes upgrading the BMS to the new DOE-SCA specification for VACnet-Tridium N4 platform at M271, Q028, Q069, Q212, and X790. The new BMS will allow DOE staff to implement improved sequence of operation programming more easily on HVAC equipment, including DCV and scheduling, which will significantly reduce energy consumption. These projects will also ensure LL87 compliance.

fms_project_name: DPR - Al Smith Windows and AC Replacement
agency_project_name: Al Smith Windows and AC Replacement
agency_project_description: Replacement of existing, single pane windows that are old and leaking and have window units in them with new, high efficiency windows and energy efficient cooling systems. Electric and steam savings due to reduced cooling and heating loads associated with envelope improvement coupled with higher efficiency cooling technology. Improved comfort conditions for building occupants. Energy savings on both cooling and heating systems and improved occupant comfort.

Domestic hot water for bathrooms and showers is provided by (1) 520 MBH AO Smith Burkay (M# HW520932) with a 200-gallon storage tank (M# TJV-200A). Water is circulated via two 1/12 HP Bell & Gosset circulators, manufactured in 1989. DSNY proposes electrifying the DHW system by replacing the existing gas water heater with (2) highly efficient Mitsubishi QAHV Heat Pump Water Heaters (M# QAHV-N136TAU) rated at 136 kBtu each. The existing storage tank is to be replaced with (2) 500-gallon storage tanks and an additional 150-gallon swing tank with resistance heating elements. The system is to contain a proprietary local BMS capable of BACnet integration. The QAHV unit coefficient of performance exceeds 4.11 in moderate weather making it an ideal choice for energy efficient water heating. Additionally, it can operate in temperatures down to -13F making it suitable for New York City's climate. The new design requirements added to comply with local laws applicable to the facility.

agency_project_name: FDNY - Multisite - ECMs at 8 Fire Houses

fms_project_name: Aeration Upgrades at Owls Head WRRF
agency_project_name: Aeration Upgrades at Owls Head WRRF
agency_project_description: This project is to upgrade the aeration system at Owls Head Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility in order to provide enough aeration to meet organics loading of future population growth projections in Owls Head's sewershed. This project has two components: 1) Replace existing ceramic dome diffusers with fine bubble membrane disc diffuser grids to increase oxygen transfer efficiency. This will enable existing blower capacity to meet 2050 demand projections.2) Implement DO control to achieve a target DO concentration of 2 mg/L throughout each bioreactor.

agency_project_description: 70 Mulberry Street Renovation project involves the major renovation of a historic building / community center in Chinatown that was destroyed by a five-alarm fire. The project involves the demolition of the current structure while ensuring the stabilization and preservation of the historic façade and stair tower. Additionally, it includes the construction of a new eight-story community center featuring a multi-purpose room intended for public athletic, performance, and recreational activities. The project will also incorporate a Building Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) façade, a green roof, and solar panels on the roof. The community center serves a diverse range of tenant groups, accommodating multiple functions such as a cafeteria, kitchen, dance studios, theater, museum storage, classrooms, terraces, and conference rooms. Additionally, the project incorporates a Percent for Art glass feature with a custom frit painting that requires a complex and challenging installation within the existing five-story stair tower.

agency_project_description: Bronx Animal Care Center & Veterinary Clinic is a new 50,000 SF facility that will be housing admissions, adoptions, medical services, and boarding for approximately 70 dogs, 140 cats, 30 rabbits and other species to be determined. The building and associated landscape are to achieve LEED Silver standards or higher.

agency_project_name: Snug Harbor Center CTR.1000 Richmond Ter.HVAC/PLU
agency_project_description: C. MAJOR DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS1. When surveying existing conditions, special attention will be paid to current building loads, layouts, and resulting possible changes in power requirements.2. The existing chilling plant is composed of one chiller installed in approximately 1982, while one other large chiller and one small chiller are not functional. Mechanical equipment and distribution system was designed and specified as per requirement of more than 30 years ago. The centralized cooling equipment (chillers) located in Building L serve 5 other buildings – Buildings M, R, S, T & G (other buildings on site either have their own air conditioning system or use window units).3. In future phase, the Main Hall/Building C Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art and Building B-SIM Natural Sciences Collection which presently do not have any central air- conditioning system will be connected to the central cooling plant. Building C and Building B along with other buildings (M, R, S, T & G) must be taken into consideration while designing the chillers and calculating the total load.4. The Snug Harbor campus will remain operational during construction therefore a detailedconstruction scheduling will be considered as high priority. The project is anticipated to be constructed in two (2) phases:• Phase 1 – Replacement of main chiller for cooling system located at Building L, and study/assessment of HVAC (steam and chilled water) pipe distribution system connecting from Building L to all served buildings.• Phase II – Replacement of all HVAC (cold and steam pipes) distribution system connecting from Building L to all served buildings. The exact scope of Phase II shall be determined on the assessment report submitted based on Phase I.

fms_project_name: Replmnt & repair of combined SE outfall north 81st &19 Ave
agency_project_name: COMBINED SEWER OUTFALL N. 81ST & 19TH AVE, LAG
agency_project_description: The proposed project involves the reconstruction and replacement of a short length of an existing sewer and an outfall that discharges into Bowery Bay (see Figures C-4a and C-4b); this sewer and outfall reconstruction is proposed to address what is currently a partially collapsed outfall. Replacement would restore the outfall’s necessary functions and avoid a potential full collapse and failure. Specifically, the proposed project includes the following: Installation of a new a 14-foot 7-inch-wide by 8-foot-high combined sewer outfall (referenced as the Bowery Bay [BB]-005 outfall) which discharges into Bowery Bay, thereby replacing the currently collapsed outfall. The proposed outfall would be reconstructed at the same location as the existing outfall and within an existing sewer easement across land that is owned by the City of New York and under the jurisdiction of the Department of Small Business Services. The proposed sewer and outfall design calls for a reinforced concrete structure supported on a concrete cradle with a flap gate at the outlet to control any inflow of tidal water from the bay. Additionally, boulders are proposed to be installed to stabilize the bottom of the bay to minimize the potential for scour and resuspension of sediments into the water column that may otherwise occur when there is flow from the outfall. Reconstruction of a 60-foot-long by 14-foot-7-inch wide and 8-foot-high combined sewer that flows into and connects with the proposed outfall.

This project includes the demolition and replacement of four air handler units (AHUs-1, 2, 3 and 6) with four new water-sourced air handler units being installed in place, removal of 10 heat pumps with new units being installed in place and the installation of 1 plate and frame heat exchanger. Associated work includes but is not limited to wiring, electrical work, duct work and plumbing to complete the installation of the new equipment. New plate frame heat exchanger/s will be installed to protect the downstream AHUs from geothermal groundwater. Integrate the new units to the existing BCM system. An existing cooling tower will be rehabilitated and put into service. Extensive mechanical piping for the entire project is required, mainly in the mechanical rooms, although a 4” pipe loop around the exterior of the building is proposed. A new solar-heat-gain shading device is included in scope to reduce base building heat in areas with single-glazed windows. Associated architectural, structural, electrical, and plumbing work, as required. It is also to meet DCAS ACE program criteria. Temporary cooling will be needed to keep the facility operation during construction.

Work includes structural modifications to and installation of elevated skywalks, including, but not limited to, adding a new skywalk, adjusting slopes of walking surfaces, extending landings, installing edge protection, and modifying adjoining protective guards and handrails. Finally, millwork and wood finishes must be repaired or replaced, in-kind, and new millwork will be required to modify existing reading areas/tiered seating, by creating multiple accessible wheelchair spaces, and adjoining companion seating.

agency_project_name: This project will reconstruct the E 169th Street step street.
agency_project_description: This capital project will address the East 169th Street step street’s substandard condition through full reconstruction of the project area. Consistent with other step street projects, the design consultant for this project shall provide several design alternatives for the project limits, with attention paid to maximizing accessibility, public space, functionality, and streetscape amenities (street trees, seating, etc.) within the right of way. DOT acknowledges that many of these priorities are competing for limited space within this constrained project site, and that the different alternatives will prioritize these competing interests differently.DOT’s preliminary accessibility analysis suggests that a combination of ADA accessible ramps and staircases are feasible within the project limits (see this document’s conceptual design attachment for a proof of concept). This scale diagram establishes that there is sufficient space for a ramp structure within the project limits. DDC shall direct the design consultant to explore various ramp and stair configurations during preliminary design and identify any technical challenges associated with their construction. If, after reviewing the design alternatives, it is determined only stairway accessibility can be provided, any technical infeasibility or other constraint that limits building to full ADA requirements must be fully documented and added to the project file. The documentation must, at a minimum, clearly lay out the issue, describe the efforts taken to rectify the issue, and explain why the final design was chosen to be selected.

The Bergen Building, located in the Tremont area of the Bronx and fronting the main pedestrian entrance of the William Gladwin Park, is composed of two separate adjacent buildings built in 1912 and 1916. In the mid-1930s, the City purchased both buildings and joined them. The building currently is leased to several not-for-profits and city agencies. The Department of Citywide Administrative Services manages and maintains the building. In 2014, DCAS, working with Mayor DeBlasio’s office identified the building as a candidate for significant energy improvements in line with the goals of the OneNYC. The City engaged Studio Gang to conduct a Pre-Schematic Design Report in anticipation of these upgrades, which detailed three levels of proposed energy improvements, bronze, silver and gold, with estimates and ambitious energy performance scope proposals.As part of this analysis, and others, major code compliance issues have been identified on the interior of the building, including travel distances, exit separation, restroom configuration and fixture counts, and accessibility issues. The building’s façade has been deficient for decades and has been determined scientifically to be a mold habitat. The fire alarm system is obsolete. Much of the wiring is original, and there is not enough electric capacity for a new HVAC system. The building requires a new sprinkler standpipe. Previous efforts to initiate Studio Gang’s proposals were underfunded. In the meantime, the building continued to degrade, and most grievously, the envelope lack of watertightness continues to take its toll.Accordingly, priority has been given to the stabilization of the envelope, as the current project initiation request makes clear. There is a budget of almost $40M to make the building watertight by replacing the roof, rehabilitating the masonry, replacing the windows, and installing a rain screen on the most porous surfaces. Critically, DCAS/Real Estate has identified required swing space to enable this work while the building remains open; new scope for this swing is included. There is cross-bracing in the rear yard which requires rehabilitation to address the façade.

fms_project_name: 280 BROADWAY - VAULT,  ELECTRICAL AND FIRE ALARM UPGRADE
agency_project_name: DCAS System Upgrade at the Sun Building Vault, MEP
agency_project_description: The Sun Building is one of the oldest buildings DCAS manages, and was designed in the Renaissance revival style.  Constructed in 1864, the building was entirely built of Tuchahoe marble and was the first modern department store built in the city.  Originally a five-story building, this seven-story building is currently home to tenants.  During a previous renovation in 2002, the fire alarm system was completely replaced, however, the electrical system was only supplemented by some new risers and panels-- a large portion of the pre-existing electrical system remained "as is" and must be upgraded.  Power monitoring must be added and emergency system (generator) must be upgraded/increased in capacity as it barely supports bare minimum life safety.  A building wide system upgrade is needed to support building tenant needs and to comply with the latest building, electrical, and fire codes and regulations.  Approximately 15% of the building (1st and 2nf floors) is occupied by private tenants and are excluded from this project.

fms_project_name: 17TH AVENUE PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE OVER BELT PARKWAY 2231300
agency_project_name: HBPK17K Pedestrian Bridge Over Belt Parkway
agency_project_description: The existing 17th Avenue and 27th Avenue Pedestrian Bridges over Belt-Parkway were constructed under the Robert Moses era Master Plan for NYC.  Because the existing 17th Avenue and 27th Avenue Pedestrian Bridges, sloping over the Belt Parkway Highway, achieve their maximum height only at the apex of their spans, they have been repeatedly impacted by errant trucks coming from the Verrazano Narrows Bridge and the Brooklyn Queens Expressway, thereby causing significant damage to the existing superstructures.  The existing bridges do not provide ADA compliant access. Due to these circumstances the existing bridges cannot be modified to meet the project goals. The total replacement will include:  precast steel grid bridge deck system, replacement of the substructure (abutments) and arch superstructure with the intention to reflect the historic design, new minimum clear width of 12’- 0” and a vertical clearance of 15’- 6”, installation of new railings, fencing, lighting, traffic signals, drainage and accessible ramps/stairway. The structure will also meet the latest Seismic code requirements and ADA compliance.

agency_project_description: The pedestrian bridge crosses the Staten Island Rapid Transit (SIRT) South Shore over Oakwood Heights Station between North Railroad Avenue and South Railroad Avenue. It was built I 1930 and no major rehabilitation took place since then.  This structure serves as a pedestrian crossing between N. Railroad Ave./St. Georg bound platform.The pedestrian bridge is 95 feet long and 6 feet wide and 4 main spans with a total deck area approximately 600 sq. ft. Spans 1-4 are the continuous main spans over the railroad trucks and platforms and Span 5seves as a stair and connects S. Railroad Ave. to the bridge. The superstructure of the main spans consists of concrete encased rolled beam multi-girder (2 girder) system with cast-in-place reinforced concrete deck supported on concrete piers.  The stair is a cast-in-place reinforced concrete slab supported on concrete footing and concrete rigid pier.

fms_project_name: GRAND CONCOURSE / METRO NORTH RR HUD2-24140-9
agency_project_name: HBX1190 Grand Concourse Bridge over Metro North Railroad Hudson Line
agency_project_description: The Grand Concourse Bridge carries four lanes of vehicular traffic and three NYC Transit No. 4 tracks beneath the roadway structure.  The Metro-North Railroad Hudson line runs under the Grand Concourse Bridge.  This project will completely replace the roadway bridge structure which was last rehabilitated in 1982 and originally constructed in 1906 (subway structure added in 1917).  Replacement of the deteriorated subway structural elements will also be a part of this project.  In addition to the bridge work, the project will also incorporate the following pedestrian improvements which are consistent with NYC’s Vision Zero and OneNYC objectives:• Curb extensions will be added at street corners to reduce the pedestrian crossing distance at both 151st and 153rd Streets and sidewalk limits will be generally be expanding throughout the project limits.• The raised concrete median in the center of Grand Concourse will be widened which will reduce pedestrian crossing distance while also creating space for a future bicycle lane.• ADA compliant pedestrian ramps will be installed at all pedestrian crossing within the project limits along with high-visibility crosswalks.• The Grand Concourse northbound 153rd Street MTA bus stop concrete island will be expanded while maintaining existing bush and tree plantings.• Street lighting was re-analyzed and the proposed design will improve on the existing lighting conditions.  All new street lights will have LED luminaires installed as well as any existing street lights that are remaining.  The proposed street lights will use historic Type M poles and luminaires to match the aesthetics of the Grand Concourse Historic District.

Replacement of Shore (Belt) Parkway Bridge over Mill Basin, Brooklyn.The project consists of the removal of the existing fourteen (14) span bascule bridge (length 864 feet) and replacement with a seventeen (17) span fixed bridge (length 2,645 feet) elevated to provide a 60 foot vertical clearance over the navigational channel. The typical bridge section consists of a composite concrete deck and steel superstructure supported on a reinforced concrete substructure on concrete piles. The new bridge will be constructed on a new alignment set on the north side of the existing bridge, partially overlapping with the existing bridge. The new bridge and approach roadways will provide three (3) 12 foot wide lanes for vehicular traffic, a 12 foot wide right shoulder on the bridge and a 10 foot wide right shoulder on the approach roadways, a minimum 4 foot wide left shoulder in each direction, and a 12 foot wide bicycle / pedestrian facility adjacent to the eastbound roadway. Substandard stopping sight distance for the bridge and approach roadways will be eliminated.  The design speed for the bridge and approach roadways is 60 MPH (100 KMPH). Necessary upland and wetland mitigation work will be performed.
